title: feat(scenarios): the external driver builds through the MCP draft door on contract objectstack-scenario-driver/2
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"hotlong"} -->
_Requested by **Jack** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EF41AQooqveF2DGD8nqPzS?thread=cmsg_01EF41AQooqveF2DGD8nqPzSPrBAnB7RiEHAGp5rsqSX3q)_

Fixes #37626

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户无感：这是内部评测工具的改动，外部智能体命令现在也能在评测里走轻门搭建应用。
- 为云端智能体效果专题服务：让云端内置智能体和 Claude Code 在同一批控制卡上打分对比。
- 出错只影响评测跑分，旧版外部命令照常跑其他模式，走轻门时会被明确拒绝，可直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

The scenario runner's external driver (`--driver external:COMMAND`) can now run door mode (`--modes door`), so the
cloud agent can be scored on the same door cards as the live `claude` driver.

- **Contract `objectstack-scenario-driver/2`** (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/drivers/external.ts`): `/1` plus an
  optional `door` on an `author` call, `{"mcp":{"url":…,"configFile":…},"skillsDir":…}`. The door's OAuth token
  travels as an `ask` call's persona key does: only in a 0600 MCP config file outside the call's directory, deleted
  when the call returns, never on argv, in the environment or on stdin. The call runs in the door task's own empty
  directory and records no files.
- **Version negotiation**: the `info` input still carries `objectstack-scenario-driver/1` (the one input both versions
  share, so a command of either version answers it); the `info` answer gains an optional `contract`. Absent means `/1`;
  a name the runner does not speak is refused, naming it. Every later input carries the version the command named,
  so a `/1` command keeps running scratch, template and ask unchanged.
- **The refusal**: the outright door refusal in `ExternalDriver.author` is replaced by a contract check
  (`assertDoor`). `main` calls it right after the driver is made, so `--modes door` with a `/1` command is refused
  before any card runs, naming the contract; `author` calls it again before it would send a door.
- **The arm**: `--door-skills` / `--door-skill-omit` reach an external command as `door.skillsDir`
  (`cwd/.claude/skills`, one directory per skill with its `SKILL.md`). Both live drivers now read the arm through one
  helper (`readDoorArm` in `door.ts`, lifted out of the `ClaudeCodeDriver` constructor), so `env.driver.door` has the
  same shape whichever driver ran. The rules arm (`--door-rules`, `OS_SCENARIOS_DOOR_RULES`) is a Claude Code
  `CLAUDE.md` and stays the `claude` driver's: refused with an external command, naming why (the variable is reported
  as unused rather than refusing the run).
- `cli.ts`: the two door-mode gates that refused every non-`claude` driver now let `external:` through to the
  contract check; Codex is still refused. `doorModeRefusal` names the external `/2` route.
- **The published constant keeps its value**: `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT` stays `objectstack-scenario-driver/1` and
  `ExternalInfoInput.contract` keeps its type, so a command that pins the constant as a literal (the cloud command's
  `scenario-driver/contract.ts` does) keeps compiling and answering. The new `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT_V2` names `/2`,
  and `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACTS` lists both.
- README: the door-mode section and the contract section state the `/2` door input for command authors (the
  consumer is objectstack-ai/cloud#5028, a cloud command implementing this contract).

## Tests

Local, on head 063eef16:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios typecheck && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios test`
  under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` → `VERDICT command-exit 0`; typecheck exit 0; Test Files 43 passed (43),
  Tests 1354 passed (1354)
- eslint `--no-inline-config` over the 9 changed `.ts`/`.mjs` files → exit 0
- New pins:
  - `test/runner/external-driver.test.ts`, describe "door mode over the external driver": `info` carries `/1` and a
    command's answered contract rides every later input; an unknown contract is refused naming it; a door author
    call's input shape, the token in the 0600 file only (fingerprint matches; not on argv, env or stdin; file outside
    `cwd`; gone after), the skills less the omission, no files recorded, the arm the record states; a no-skills door
    call; a `/1` command refused by `assertDoor` and by `author` with no process started; the command line
    (`--door-skills` reaches the command, `--door-rules` refused naming why, Codex still refused).
  - `test/runner/door.test.ts`: the external driver's arm equals the `claude` driver's for the same flags.
  - `test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts`, describe "door mode through an external command on contract `/2`": a full door
    run of the crm card through the stand-in command — built through the door, published, graded; the command read
    the token from a 0600 file only; the record, the recording, the scorecard and the gallery export hold no token;
    and the CLI (`main`) refusing `--modes door` with a `/1` command before any card runs, nothing scaffolded, no turn
    sent.
  - `test/runner/external-driver.test.ts`: `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT` still reads `objectstack-scenario-driver/1`.
- Ablation (each committed first, restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, `git status --porcelain` empty after):
  putting the token on the door input turns the door-author pin red (`expected [ 'configFile', 'token', 'url' ] to
  deeply equal [ 'configFile', 'url' ]`); dropping the contract check in `doorAuthor` turns the `/1` pin red
  (`promise resolved … instead of rejecting`); dropping the `assertDoor` call in `cli.ts` `main` turns the CLI pin red
  (the run goes on past the gate and the case times out).

## Acceptance notes

- **Card premise, re-measured on `origin/main` 33a31dc7**: the refusal was at `external.ts:307` as stated. Two more
  gates of the same refusal were in `cli.ts` (`makeDriver`'s door-flag check and `main`'s door-mode check); both are
  in this diff. `door.ts:290-293` is the refusal text, not the arm's shape; the arm's shape is `DoorArm` (same file),
  which this diff makes both drivers build through `readDoorArm`.
- **Publication**: `@objectstack/scenarios` (the order's `@objectstack/qa`) is published to npm with the `./runner`
  export, which re-exports `drivers/external.ts`; `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT` keeps `/1` and `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT_V2`
  is added, and the contract is stated in the published README. The change is additive for command authors (a `/1` command runs as before); the
  seat re-declared it `Clause-②: yes` (a backward-compatible widening of a published contract), in this body and the
  changeset.
- **Not enforced for an external command**: the README asks a door command to build through the door alone; the
  runner denies the `claude` driver's door turn every file and command tool but cannot see inside an external
  command, and the README says so (it grades only what the publish serves either way).
- **Not in this diff**: the rules arm for an external command. The contract carries no rules; a later version could
  carry the rendered rules as a file path if the cloud command wants them.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/runner/external-driver.test.ts -t "door mode over the external driver"` → 6 passed.

Read first: `src/runner/drivers/external.ts` (`doorAuthor`, the `info` negotiation), `src/runner/cli.ts` (the two
gates and the `assertDoor` call), `README.md` (the contract section).

<details><summary>Derived gate families (local subset)</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` on this branch: 65 commands. 62 exit 0 on head 98e8f7e5 (before the merge of `origin/main`, which touched no gate input of this diff). Not measured locally, both
for environmental prerequisites, left to CI: `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` (exit 3: its
pinned positive control is unreachable from this shallow clone) and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3:
PREREQUISITE NOT MET, the repo is not fully built here). `pnpm check:type-check-debt` (it builds and type-checks the whole workspace) was still running when this body was written; its verdict is in the report comment, and CI runs it.

`node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs --branch=HEAD` → `VERDICT clean exit 0` (origin/main merges cleanly; no open PR
shares a file).

</details>
